title: Underived continuous functions compute derived internal functions of profinite parameters
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extending norm topology. Put $F=E$ and $A_F(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Use the small coherent profinite site in [def-weil-size-convention], its ordinary internal $A_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and ordinary derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For a profinite set $P$ in these universes, let $A_F[P]$ be the free internal $A_F$-module on $\underline P(S)=C(S,P)$; this is the left adjoint to forgetting modules to condensed sets. Let $\mathcal C_F(P)$ be the internal module whose sections on $S$ are $C(S\times P,F)$, with $A_F(S)$ acting through the $S$-coordinate. Evaluation identifies it with $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{A_F}(A_F[P],A_F)$, where internal module Hom is the right adjoint of internal tensor. Derive this Hom in its second variable by nonnegative injective resolutions. The canonical resolution comparison is an isomorphism
$$\mathcal C_F(P)[0]\longrightarrow R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{A_F}(A_F[P],A_F[0])$$
in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_F})$. It is natural contravariantly in every continuous map of profinite parameter sets and its degree-zero map is the evaluation identification just specified. The coefficient field $F=E$ is complete. All continuous functions are retained; no restriction to locally constant functions is imposed.

proof.text: Put $A=A_F$. Use the internal-to-sectionwise equivalence in [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] on the small coherent profinite site. Its hypotheses hold for the sheafified abelian tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. It leaves sections, restrictions and the regular coefficient module unchanged. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] it is exact and preserves tensor, hence identifies right adjoints by their adjunction bijections. The sectionwise tensor right adjoint is exactly the slice sheaf Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom], by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]; thus this is the transported internal Hom. The abelian sheaf category is Grothendieck, with additive closed tensor, by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] applied to $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Ab}$. The internal module category is consequently Grothendieck by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], so [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] supplies a nonnegative injective resolution $A\to I^\bullet$. An exact equivalence preserves injectivity, since its inverse carries monomorphisms to monomorphisms and its Hom bijections carry the injective lifting property to the same property. We may therefore compute in sectionwise $A$-modules.

source.place: Tags 08J7 and 03FD (injective module resolutions), and sites-modules.tex Tag 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor), for the sheaf-Hom identification

proof.text: For an $A$-module $N$ and a profinite $S$, the definition [def-pur-sheaf-hom] gives $\mathcal Hom_A(A[P],N)(S)=\operatorname{Hom}_{A|_S}(A[P]|_S,N|_S)$. A map on the right is specified by the image of the universal generator: it is a section $x\in N(S\times P)$. Explicitly a generator over $U\to S$ given by $p:U\to P$ is sent to $(U\to S\times P)^*x$, and a linear combination $\sum_i a_i[p_i]$ is sent to $\sum_i a_i(U\to S\times P)^*_ix$. Conversely evaluating on the tautological $P$-coordinate of $S\times P$ recovers $x$. These operations are inverse, natural in $N,S,P$, and respect sheafification by the defining universal property of the free internal module $A[P]$. Thus the complex $J^\bullet=\mathcal Hom_A(A[P],I^\bullet)$ has $J^n(S)=I^n(S\times P)$, with the same differentials. At $N=A$ this gives $C(S\times P,F)$, and scalar multiplication uses the $S$-coordinate. By derivation in the second variable using the chosen nonnegative injective resolution, $J^\bullet$ represents the required derived Hom. The comparison map on $S$ is $A(S\times P)[0]\to I^\bullet(S\times P)$ induced by the resolution augmentation.

source.place: Tag 08J7, definition of derived sheaf Hom and the free-module evaluation identification

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F$ be the underlying abelian sheaf of $A$, so $\mathcal F(V)=C(V,F)$. For a finite jointly surjective cover $\{T_i\to V\}$, form the continuous surjection $q:T=\coprod_iT_i\to V$. Apply [lem-sfb-normed-scalar-profinite-cech-exact] to $q$. Each fibre power $T_V^{n+1}$ is the finite disjoint union of $(T_{i_0}\times_V\cdots\times_VT_{i_n})$ over tuples of indices. A function on this disjoint union is continuous exactly when its restrictions are continuous. Therefore its function group is the product of the groups in degree $n$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Omitting coordinates has the corresponding tuple-of-indices restrictions, so the differential is precisely the alternating Cech differential. The cited analytic exactness says that every positive Cech cocycle for this cover is a coboundary, hence its positive Cech cohomology vanishes.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2)–(4), finite complete E case; agent passage from the analytic Cech lemma to finite covering families

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] to this coherent profinite site with $\mathcal B$ all its objects and $\mathrm{Cov}$ all its defining finite jointly surjective covering families. Every iterated fibre product is profinite, so lies in $\mathcal B$. These families are the coverings in the defining pretopology, hence cofinal as required; equivalently any generated covering sieve contains such a family. Step 3 verifies the positive Cech-vanishing hypothesis for every member of $\mathrm{Cov}$. We obtain $H^q(V,\mathcal F)=0$ for all profinite $V$ and $q>0$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison], for the actual ring sheaf $A$, identifies $H^q(I^\bullet(V))$ with these abelian-sheaf groups and identifies degree zero with $A(V)$. Its smallness and enough-injectives hypotheses were checked in Step 1; it imposes no constant-ring condition; completeness of E is used only in the analytic input of Step 3. In particular $A(S\times P)[0]\to I^\bullet(S\times P)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of abelian-group complexes for every $S$.

By Steps 2 and 4 the augmentation $\mathcal C_F(P)[0]\to J^\bullet$ is exact on section complexes on every profinite test object. For each positive degree, the presheaf kernel equals the presheaf image; at degree zero its kernel is the image of $\mathcal C_F(P)$. Thus these presheaf images are already the corresponding kernel sheaves, so the same equality holds for sheaf images. This proves that the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism of module sheaves, hence an isomorphism after derived localization [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For a continuous $v:P'\to P$, the map between section complexes is restriction along $1_S\times v$. It commutes with $I^\bullet$'s differentials and augmentation by naturality of the resolution maps as sheaf maps. The free-generator description in Step 2 identifies this map with precomposition by $A[P']\to A[P]$. Consequently the square of comparison chain maps commutes before localization and therefore afterwards. In degree zero it sends $f(s,p)$ to $f(s,v(p'))$, exactly the prescribed evaluation identification and its parameter naturality. All arguments used $C(-,F)$ itself.

source.place: Tag 08J7, the fixed augmentation and functoriality of restriction in the Hom-complex model

It answers the E2 RETURN of 6f0dfe97, and every point of that RETURN is repaired. (1) Statement: both nodes now take F=E, any finite extension of Q_ell, with the report section 'Source error'. I verified the Omega counterexample myself: on the Cantor set, with T=beta(S_disc) and an alpha-orthogonal basis, f=W(y)-W(x) is an Omega-valued Cech 1-cocycle, and a primitive would give h with h-w in Omega; Baire gives a point with infinitely many nonzero coordinates. Steps: the Grothendieck chain (Step 1), Hom(A[P]|_S,N|_S)=N(S x P) by Yoneda on the slice (Step 2), the Cech identification over the disjoint union of the cover (Step 3), the general-site Cech criterion hypotheses (1)-(3) and the arbitrary-ring module/abelian comparison (Step 4), and the sectionwise quasi-isomorphism and naturality in P (Step 5) all hold. The new node lem-sfb-normed-scalar-profinite-cech-exact is true for E: Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 4.3.9(2)-(4) with G=1 and Lemma 4.3.7 give H^i(S,C(-,E))=0 for i>0, and applied to the fibre powers this gives Cech exactness.
